artigo.texto: Materials scientists have demonstrated that integrating natural volcanic black iron sand into graphene-based electrodes can dramatically amplify the electrochemical performance of flexible supercapacitors, offering an abundant and environmentally sustainable pathway for high-capacity energy storage. The experimental investigation established that incorporating this mineral-rich sand into supercapacitor architectures yielded exceptional charge-storage capabilities when paired with either an acidic polymer gel electrolyte or natural seawater. Devices engineered with black iron sand and a polyvinyl alcohol and phosphoric acid electrolyte mixture achieved a specific capacitance of 668.66 farads per gram and an energy density of 92.7 watt-hours per kilogram, outperforming baseline graphene devices lacking the sand additive by more than sevenfold. Even when operated using raw, untreated seawater as a safe and non-toxic aqueous electrolyte, the black sand supercapacitors attained a specific capacitance of 282.24 farads per gram alongside an energy density of 39.2 watt-hours per kilogram. The global proliferation of portable consumer electronics, including mobile smartphones, tablets, and wearable smartwatches, has established a relentless technical requirement for energy storage components capable of sustained operating lifespans. Commercial electronics rely almost exclusively on lithium-ion batteries, which provide high volumetric energy capacity but exhibit severe functional constraints that restrict their long-term applicability. Supercapacitors have surfaced as an appealing alternative, storing electrical charge simultaneously through electrostatic electrical double-layer capacitance and rapid faradaic redox interactions. Although supercapacitors offer exceptionally rapid recharging rates, simple structural designs, lightweight configurations, and exceptional cycle stability extending to tens of thousands of continuous operational cycles, standard carbon-based configurations have traditionally suffered from modest total energy density that restricts their utilization in extended operating scenarios. Previous scientific initiatives aimed at overcoming the intrinsic energy density limitations of supercapacitors have extensively investigated synthetic transition metal oxides, complex nickel compounds, and engineered nanostructured composites. Researchers had earlier synthesized porous nickel cobalt oxide nanostructures via spray pyrolysis, achieving specific capacitances approaching 676.82 farads per gram and delivering high energy densities in asymmetric cell formats, while other investigations examined nickel oxide films deposited using distinct organic solvent matrices. Concurrently, carbon nanomaterials such as pristine graphene, nitrogen-doped graphene sheets, and graphene oxide membranes have been widely studied due to graphene’s remarkable theoretical specific surface area of 2630 square meters per gram, high electrical conductivity, and low density of 2.28 grams per cubic centimeter. Composite formulations incorporating synthetic silica nanoparticles or laboratory-precipitated magnetite nanoparticles have similarly demonstrated viable capacitance retention and reversible iron oxidation kinetics. The current investigation deliberately circumvents these fabrication barriers by sourcing unrefined, naturally synthesized volcanic minerals directly from coastal environments. The natural volcanic black iron sand evaluated in this work was gathered from the coastal shoreline of Playa El Real, situated within the municipality of Tecoman in Colima, Mexico. The raw mineral sand was subjected to an initial physical screening, washing, and filtration routine to remove residual organic debris, after which it was thoroughly dehydrated in a laboratory drying oven. To construct flexible supercapacitor electrodes, the investigators utilized flexible substrates made from recycled polyethylene plastic cut into rectangular strips measuring 2.0 centimeters by 3.0 centimeters. A conductive foundation layer of commercial graphene ink was deposited onto the recycled polymer backing using a precision blade-coating technique, creating baseline graphene electrodes. Copper foil collector strips were subsequently attached to ensure electrical contact, after which the finely ground volcanic black sand redox powder was blade-coated directly over the graphene layer to form composite electrodes possessing a uniform redox layer thickness of 70 micrometers and an active mineral mass of 65 milligrams alongside 5.7 milligrams of graphene. Extensive microscopic and crystallographic characterization verified the structural composition and mineral distribution across the fabricated electrode interfaces. Scanning electron microscopy of the underlying graphene foundation revealed densely stacked microplates measuring approximately 2.0 by 3.5 micrometers, which formed continuous, interconnected electrical conduction pathways despite localized microcracks and surface pinholes typical of blade-coated carbon coatings. Microscopic examination of the black sand powder demonstrated mineral grains averaging 3.5 micrometers across, which dispersed across the dark graphene base to establish a multi-scale, textured active topography. X-ray diffraction patterns confirmed the coexistence of distinct crystalline minerals on the electrode surface. Characteristic diffraction peaks matching standard crystallographic references confirmed the dominant presence of crystalline silicon dioxide and magnetite phases, along with reflections corresponding to the polyethylene substrate, metallic aluminum impurities originating from the recycled plastic base, calcite calcium carbonate minerals, and the characteristic (002) graphitic carbon reflection centered at 26.6 degrees two-theta. artigo.texto: 2 min leitura Greenvolt constrói projeto solar e de armazenamento de energia nos EUA O projeto, que conta com um investimento de mais de 120 milhões de dólares deverá estar concluído até ao verão de 2028. Este vai ser o maior empreendimento de energia solar e armazenamento em baterias da empresa no país. 25 Nov 2026 - 15:42 2 min leitura A Greenvolt começou a construir um projeto solar combinado com um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias, num investimento acima de 120 milhões de dólares (109 milhões de euros) no sul dos EUA, divulgou hoje a empresa. “Combinando 100 MWac de produção solar com um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) de 50 MW [megawatt] / 200 MWh [megawatt-hora], o projeto representa um investimento superior a 120 milhões de dólares (aproximadamente 109 milhões de euros) e constitui um passo importante no desenvolvimento contínuo da atividade da Greenvolt nos Estados Unidos”, refere a empresa em comunicado. No documento, a energética refere que o projeto, denominado Alamogordo, está a ser construído pela Greenvolt Power, empresa do grupo dedicada a projetos de energias renováveis de grande escala. O projeto situa-se no condado de Otero, no estado norte-americano do Novo México e deverá estar totalmente construído até ao verão de 2028, ficando a ser o maior projeto combinado de energia solar e armazenamento de energia em baterias da empresa no país. A Greenvolt acrescenta que assegurou um contrato de aquisição de energia de longo prazo para a venda de eletricidade produzida, garantindo-lhe “receitas contratualizadas e previsibilidade financeira durante um período alargado”. A empresa explica que o sistema de baterias permite armazenar eletricidade “durante um período máximo de quatro horas”, o que possibilitará disponibilizar esta energia produzida durante os períodos de maior produção solar, “maximizando o seu valor e promovendo uma utilização mais flexível das energias renováveis”. Citado no documento, o presidente executivo da Greenvolt, João Manso Neto, garantiu que os EUA vão assumir “um papel cada vez mais importante na concretização do plano de negócios do grupo”, que conta com 341 MW de energia eólica, 686 MW de energia solar e 212 MW de capacidade de armazenamento de energia em baterias. A Greenvolt regista ainda que os trabalhos de engenharia, aprovisionamento e construção são assegurados pela CJR Renewables e pela Dashiell Corporation, estimando criar 370 postos de trabalho durante esta fase. artigo.texto: Petrobras avalia extração e refino de minerais críticos para baterias Novo plano de negócios da estatal detalha oportunidades de investimento na cadeia produtiva de baterias, da prospecção mineral à reciclagem A Petrobras avalia investimentos na prospecção, extração e refino de minerais críticos voltados à cadeia produtiva de baterias. A estratégia foi detalhada no Plano de Negócios 2027-2031 da estatal, aprovado na última segunda-feira (23). Embora o interesse da petroleira por minerais críticos não seja novo, a companhia passou a detalhar as etapas da cadeia produtiva em que considera investir, diante da perspectiva de expansão da demanda por veículos elétricos e sistemas de armazenamento de energia. No plano anterior, baterias e minerais críticos figuravam entre as apostas tecnológicas de longo prazo da estatal, dentro de seu portfólio de pesquisa e desenvolvimento. Agora, a Petrobras destaca a “maior valorização de minerais críticos como ativos estratégicos para segurança energética e industrial”. Além das atividades de mineração e refino mineral, a companhia avalia investimentos na montagem de conjuntos de baterias, em sistemas de armazenamento estacionário de energia, infraestrutura de recarga de veículos elétricos, reúso e reciclagem. A montagem de células de baterias, por sua vez, aparece como uma frente de pesquisa e desenvolvimento. A estatal pretende priorizar oportunidades que apresentem maior sinergia com seus negócios no setor energético. A Petrobras também considera favorável o ambiente regulatório brasileiro, citando a recente publicação do decreto que define os minerais críticos e estratégicos para o país, incluindo aqueles utilizados na cadeia de armazenamento de energia. Entre os principais minerais utilizados na fabricação de baterias estão o lítio, o níquel e o grafite, dos quais o Brasil possui reservas relevantes. A eventual entrada da Petrobras nessas atividades faz parte da estratégia de diversificação dos negócios da companhia, que busca ampliar sua atuação em segmentos relacionados à transição energética. O documento, entretanto, não especifica quais minerais deverão ser priorizados pela estatal, nem os valores que poderão ser destinados ao segmento. As oportunidades de investimento ainda estão em fase de avaliação. A possível entrada da Petrobras no setor mineral ocorre em meio a discussões dentro do governo federal sobre a necessidade de ampliar a participação de empresas brasileiras na exploração de minerais críticos e estratégicos. Uma ala do Executivo defende uma atuação mais direta da estatal no segmento, diante do avanço de empresas estrangeiras sobre ativos minerais brasileiros. A preocupação é que o país fique restrito ao fornecimento de matérias-primas, sem capturar parte relevante do valor agregado nas etapas de processamento e industrialização. Em agosto, o presidente do BNDES (Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social), Aloizio Mercadante, defendeu publicamente uma maior participação da Vale e da Petrobras no desenvolvimento das cadeias produtivas de minerais críticos e terras raras no Brasil.

artigo.texto: ACME Solar Commissions 63.78 MW Battery Storage Project in Rajasthan; Shares Rise 0.17% Authored By HDFC SKY | Last Modified: Nov 26, 2026 10:07 AM IST ACME Solar Holdings Limited has commissioned 63.78 MW/255.12 MWh of discharge capacity from its Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. The project, developed through its wholly owned subsidiary ACME Hybrid Urja Private Limited, forms part of a larger 280 MW/1,120 MWh storage component associated with an NHPC power project. Commercial operations for the commissioned capacity are scheduled to begin on November 27, 2026. ACME Solar shares traded marginally higher during morning trading on November 26. Open Free Demat Account Mumbai, November 26: ACME Solar Holdings Limited has announced the commissioning of 63.78 MW/255.120 MWh of discharge capacity under its Battery Energy Storage System project in Rajasthan. The capacity was commissioned on November 25, 2026, through its wholly owned subsidiary, ACME Hybrid Urja Private Limited. The project is part of the NHPC Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) Power Project in Jaisalmer district. ACME Solar shares traded around ₹417.40 during Thursday’s morning session, marginally above the previous closing price. ACME Solar Commissions 63.78 MW/255.12 MWh BESS Capacity at NHPC Project According to the company’s November 26 regulatory filing, ACME Hybrid Urja Private Limited has commissioned the battery storage capacity at Village Mehar Nagar, Tehsil Pokaran, District Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. The newly commissioned portion has a discharge capacity of 63.78 MW/255.120 MWh and an installed capacity of 63.78 MW/300 MWh. This capacity forms part of the larger BESS component of the NHPC FDRE Power Project, which has a planned discharge capacity of 280 MW/1,120 MWh and an installed capacity of 280 MW/1,316 MWh. ACME Solar confirmed that only the battery energy storage component covered by the latest disclosure has been commissioned. The announcement does not represent completion of the entire renewable energy project. The commercial operation date for the newly commissioned capacity is scheduled for November 27, 2026. The company has already signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with NHPC Limited for the project. Battery energy storage systems allow electricity generated from renewable sources to be stored and supplied when required, helping improve power availability and support electricity grid stability. The latest commissioning adds to ACME Solar’s operational storage capacity and marks further progress in developing its renewable energy and battery storage infrastructure. Stock Market Snapshot ACME Solar Holdings share price were trading at approximately ₹417.40 on Thursday, November 26, 2026, up ₹0.70 or 0.17% from the previous NSE closing price of ₹416.70 on November 25. The supplied chart shows the stock trading around ₹417 at the beginning of the morning session. After regular trading began at 9:15 AM, shares briefly declined towards ₹415 before recovering above the previous closing price. The stock subsequently moved towards ₹417.80 before easing slightly to trade around ₹417.40. The chart extends to approximately 9:31 AM IST. The quoted share price and percentage movement are approximate because an exact last-traded timestamp is not displayed. ACME Solar shares had gained 1.24% in the previous session on November 25. Thursday’s marginal increase followed that positive close. The latest battery storage commissioning represents an operational milestone, although its direct contribution to the stock’s morning movement has not been independently established. About ACME Solar Holdings ACME Solar Holdings Limited is a Gurugram-headquartered renewable energy company engaged in developing, constructing and operating clean energy projects across India. The company’s portfolio includes solar power, wind energy, hybrid renewable energy and battery energy storage systems. ACME Solar develops projects under long-term power purchase agreements with electricity utilities and other power procurement agencies. Conclusion ACME Solar Holdings has commissioned 63.78 MW/255.120 MWh of battery discharge capacity at its NHPC FDRE project in Rajasthan, with commercial operations scheduled to begin on November 27, 2026. The development marks further progress in the company’s renewable energy storage expansion. Shares traded marginally higher during morning trading on November 26, although the commissioning announcement’s direct impact on the stock price remains unconfirmed. artigo.texto: Uzbekistan will receive an $8.5mn grant to expand climate cooperation with South Korea under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, the Ministry of Economy and Finance has reported. The relevant documents were signed on November 25 during a meeting between Deputy Minister of Economy and Finance Umid Abidxadjayev and representatives of the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) and the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI). The project aims to establish a framework for cooperation between Uzbekistan and South Korea in the international carbon market. This will include developing procedures, guidelines and a joint action plan for carbon credit trading. The grant will also finance the establishment of a specialized training center to prepare professionals to develop and manage carbon projects. In addition, pilot projects will be implemented in agriculture, energy and water management to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The initiative is expected to strengthen Uzbekistan's capacity to participate in international carbon markets and support its efforts to meet climate targets. In 2025, KOICA provided financial support to GGGI for an investment project aimed at the green recovery of the Aral Sea region. The initiative focused on developing climate-resilient agriculture in Karakalpakstan, introducing water-saving technologies and attracting green investment. On November 17, the BRICS-founded New Development Bank signed a $300mn loan agreement to finance the first phase of a project to develop Uzbekistan's low-carbon energy sector. The funding is set to support solar, wind, hydropower and nuclear energy projects.

artigo.texto: O governo Lula ainda não publicou o decreto que regulamenta o Redata, regime que isenta data centers de impostos na compra de equipamentos, dois meses depois de a lei ter sido sancionada em 15 de setembro. Parte do benefício vale até 31 de dezembro. Por que o decreto ainda não saiu A regulamentação ficou represada porque o governo priorizou, em novembro, as discussões sobre transição energética para a COP31. A ministra da Casa Civil, Miriam Belchior, informou na sexta-feira (6 de novembro) que o anúncio viria só depois da viagem do presidente à conferência do clima e à Cúpula da Asean. Agora o impasse é outro. O governo discute se o gás natural pode ser enquadrado como fonte de baixa emissão para cumprir a contrapartida de energia limpa que a lei exige dos data centers. Ministérios da Fazenda, da Casa Civil e de Minas e Energia discutem o tema há semanas, e a tendência é que o gás acabe incluído no texto final. Defensores do combustível argumentam que ele serve de transição para evitar a instabilidade de fontes intermitentes, como solar e eólica. Críticos afirmam que a medida contraria metas de descarbonização e pode prejudicar a competitividade do país na atração de empresas de tecnologia. O Redata suspende por até cinco anos o Imposto de Importação sobre equipamentos sem produção nacional equivalente. Publicidade Já o desconto de PIS/Cofins e IPI, o mais usado pelas empresas que já compram servidores, só vale até 31 de dezembro deste ano. Na cerimônia de sanção, em setembro, o secretário-executivo do Ministério da Fazenda, Rogério Ceron, disse que a medida busca reduzir a dependência do país de infraestrutura estrangeira: "o país se torne competitivo em relação ao mundo. E isso é importante porque envolve soberania". O benefício tem contrapartida. Para usar o regime, o data center precisa destinar ao menos 10% da capacidade de processamento ao mercado nacional, manter eficiência hídrica de até 0,05 litro de água por kWh e investir 2% do valor dos equipamentos em pesquisa no país. Nas regiões Norte, Nordeste e Centro-Oeste, essas exigências caem para 8% e 1,6%. O governo já havia tratado o Redata como aposta de peso. Em setembro, Lula disse que o regime poderia atrair R$ 500 bilhões em investimentos no país. Dois meses depois de sancionar a lei, o decreto que faria esse dinheiro sair do papel segue indefinido. O que acontece agora Sem data confirmada para o decreto, o relógio corre para o fim do ano. Se a regulamentação não sair até 31 de dezembro, as empresas perdem o desconto de PIS/Cofins e IPI deste ano, e só resta a suspensão do Imposto de Importação, válida por cinco anos. O impasse sobre o gás natural tende a definir o texto final. Enquanto isso, o projeto de hub de data centers de IA também trava no Congresso, em outra frente da mesma disputa sobre energia e investimento estrangeiro no setor.

artigo.texto: By Staff Reporter | A new data center planning to break ground in Cochise County next year is facing some resistance from Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes. Mayes asked county officials to delay their Dec. 9 vote on Tombstone Resources, the company name used to request a special use permit for Cochise SuperComputer Campus, a proposed SpaceX data center. The attorney general advised the Cochise County Planning and Zoning Commission to provide the residents of the county with more answers on the project prior to deciding whether or not to grant SpaceX a special use permit. In a request letter to the commission, Mayes echoed the estimate that the proposed data center would consume an energy equivalent to nearly 20% of the state’s total power generating capacity. “SpaceX’s proposal raises serious questions about energy reliability, water use, emergency response capabilities, traffic impacts, and more,” said Mayes. Mayes advised the officials that the scope of these concerns warranted full examination from state and federal agencies prior to local approval. SpaceX promised to contribute $50 billion in the region’s essential local services, public education, infrastructure, and other undisclosed public goods. The company also stated that it would complete a biological and special-status species assessment before breaking ground. According to SpaceX, the data center campus was designed to not disrupt the natural migratory patterns for sandhill cranes — Cochise County is a recognized wintering area for these birds — and that their company would survey for nesting birds, raptors, and burrowing owls. In conversations with Frank Antenori, chair of the Cochise County Board of Supervisors, SpaceX reiterated their promise to spend $3.6 billion to upgrade the power grid, not rely on groundwater to run the facility, and adhere to the county’s rules on light pollution. SpaceX says the campus will rely on closed-loop cooling, a dry-cooled system with no evaporation spray. Antenori told AZ Family that SpaceX estimated the data center would bring “about 1,000 jobs,” around half only requiring a high school diploma or GED, in addition to 1,500 secondary jobs. SpaceX projects that the data center will bring up to $103 million in new annual property tax revenue, and up to $250 million in a one-time county sales tax benefit. The company also projected a 10% to 40% decrease in electricity bills for all Sulphur Springs Valley Electric Cooperative members for the life of the data center development, and an additional annual benefit to those members of approximately $260 million to be used for residential bill relief, the Sulphur Springs Valley Electric Cooperative Foundation, and new capital credits for all members. If approved, the data center would become one of the largest in existence in the U.S. It would take up approximately 750 acres of land to house nine supercomputing buildings, each around 500,000 square feet. SpaceX appears confident that the county will approve its special use permit request. Their webpage reports that construction will begin in 2027. Mayes announced a town hall for residents to discuss the proposed data center, scheduled for Thursday, Dec. 3 from 5:30 to 7 p.m. AZ Free News is your #1 source for Arizona news and politics. artigo.texto: A Comissão Federal de Comunicações dos Estados Unidos (FCC) autorizou nesta quarta-feira (25) a SpaceX, empresa aeroespacial de Elon Musk, a implantar uma constelação de até 1 milhão de satélites equipados para funcionar como data centers em órbita terrestre. É a primeira vez, na história do país, que o regulador aprova uma constelação desse tipo. A constelação se chamará Starmind e será alimentada por energia solar. O objetivo é ampliar a capacidade de processamento para a inteligência artificial e reduzir o consumo de recursos terrestres. Os equipamentos vão processar grandes quantidades de dados no espaço, mas continuarão atendendo a demandas na Terra. A proposta da empresa é aproveitar a energia solar e o espaço disponível em órbita para diminuir o consumo de água e eletricidade das instalações tradicionais. O presidente da FCC, Brendan Carr, disse que a decisão abre uma nova fronteira tecnológica. Segundo a FCC, o projeto deve ajudar a atender à demanda crescente por capacidade de processamento. Cada satélite terá capacidade computacional média de 175 quilowatts, podendo alcançar 250 quilowatts. Os equipamentos terão a função de processar dados utilizados no planeta. A autorização é válida até 2040, segundo documento publicado no site do órgão regulador. A liberação não garante o lançamento imediato dos satélites, que depende do cumprimento de etapas e prazos exigidos pela FCC. A SpaceX conta com foguetes próprios, que já realizaram centenas de missões.

artigo.texto: The transaction secures capital against contracted, insured delivery of durable removals, proof that high-integrity projects can now access scalable debt beyond equity. State of Sao Paulo, Brazil--(Newsfile Corp. - November 24, 2026) - InPlanet and Idemitsu Americas Holdings (IAH), a wholly owned subsidiary of Idemitsu Kosan (Idemitsu), today announced the closing of one of the first non-recourse project financings in the Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) sector. InPlanet and Idemitsu Americas Holdings Close Non-Recourse Debt Facility, Setting a New Standard for Financing ERW Carbon Removal. To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit: https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/8814/324893_f9020ca7c4c68ba6_002full.jpg The debt facility will fund the delivery of more than 28,500 tonnes of contracted Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) and is structured to be repeatable, providing a template for how institutional capital can finance verified CDR at scale. Financing Carbon Removal at Scale Gigaton-scale carbon removal requires financing that can scale deployment beyond equity alone. This agreement was designed to do that, with downside protection backed by an existing carbon removal agreement to remove more than 28,500 tonnes of CO₂ between 2026 and 2028. The financing also includes carbon delivery insurance provided by CFC, covering specified project delivery risks for a defined portion of the delivery. CFC is a specialist insurance provider supporting high-quality carbon market transactions, and the Howden Broking Group provided broking service to InPlanet for this transaction. The financing decision was supported by InPlanet's operating track record, including more than 200,000 tonnes of silicate rock applied across Brazilian farmland. This delivery is enabled by Bedrock OS, InPlanet's AI-powered operating infrastructure, which supports project execution across its portfolio and consolidates logistics, farm, and laboratory data into auditable records for reporting. Each project strengthens the underlying dataset and AI models used to optimize delivery and scale ERW. To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit: https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/8814/324893_f9020ca7c4c68ba6_003full.jpg By linking capital to contracted demand, insured delivery, and the operational infrastructure required to execute at scale, the structure demonstrates how high-integrity carbon removal can be financed like infrastructure and replicated across projects, regions, and buyers as the market matures. For Idemitsu, the partnership forms part of a broader strategy to expand its role in carbon markets as it works toward a carbon-neutral society by 2050. As global demand grows for permanent, measurable, and verifiable removal solutions, Idemitsu is deepening its engagement with durable CDR pathways, with ERW emerging as an area of focus due to its potential for scale. "InPlanet's work in Brazil combines scientific rigor with real operating scale, which is what durable carbon removal needs in order to move beyond pilots,"said Masanori Abe, President of Idemitsu Americas Holdings Corporation." By linking capital to contracted demand and insured delivery, this agreement demonstrates a financing approach we expect to be repeatable. IAH looks forward to building on it as we expand our CDR business." Today, InPlanet operates Brazil's largest ERW program by farmland treated, with access to more than 100,000 hectares through its partners. Working with farmers nationwide, InPlanet applies finely ground silicate rock to agricultural land, accelerating a natural process that permanently captures atmospheric carbon while restoring soil fertility, reducing chemical input costs, and strengthening long-term farm profitability. In December 2024, InPlanet delivered the world's first independently verified ERW carbon removal credits, which subsequently received a post-issuance "A" rating from BeZero Carbon. "In just two years, we went from delivering the world's first independently verified enhanced rock weathering credits to operating the largest ERW program in Brazil. This financing with Idemitsu takes that work to its next level, it shows that carbon removal grounded in solid science can also be financed like real infrastructure," said Felix Harteneck, Founder & CEO of InPlanet. "For us, this is about more than capital. Japan is continuing to develop its carbon market and standards for high-integrity carbon removal, and we look forward to contributing to that dialogue." Compliance Demand in Japan and Brazil Idemitsu and InPlanet will focus on markets where climate ambition and carbon market infrastructure are advancing in step. Japan is continuing to develop its carbon market framework and policies supporting high-integrity carbon removal. Any future use of ERW credits would remain subject to applicable methodologies, regulations, and eligibility requirements. In Brazil, Law 15.042/2024 established the SBCE (Brazilian Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading System), putting removals on the same legal footing as avoided emissions. Both markets are opening compliance pathways for durable carbon removal, creating long-term, regulated demand for credits that have until now relied almost entirely on voluntary buyers. artigo.texto: CHAMPAIGN — A proposed development just east of the Interstate 57/74 interchange that includes a solar farm, battery storage systems and two small data centers has attracted the concern of a nearby business owner. “It’s an eyesore for one thing, but it’s also a danger,” said Judy Parkinson, co-owner of Research Press Publishers. “The data centers and the batteries are my big concern. Those are not the kind of thing you should have in such a close-to-the-city area. If they did it out in the countryside, it wouldn’t bother me.” She fears that the battery energy storage systems could be a fire hazard that might impact her business if a blaze breaks out. IAG Investments — Champaign Mattis LLC, which is managed by Anthony Donato, seeks to develop approximately 30 acres of vacant land at 2703 N. Mattis Ave. into an industrial site that includes “flex warehouses and a solar farm with accessory battery energy storage systems,” said city of Champaign Associate Planner Mia Trevino. As previously reported by The News-Gazette’s Kathy Reiser, Anthony Donato and Donato Solar have developed several other solar arrays with data farms in and around Champaign-Urbana in recent years. The solar farms are run by Donato Solar and the data centers are operated by Gail Technology. Anthony Donato founded the former company and is the owner of the latter. “The proposed site plan includes five commercial flex warehouses with 3,000 square feet of data centers in proposed Buildings 1 and 5 that are 1.2 (megawatts), approximately 60 percent of the respective buildings’ area,” Trevino wrote in a report to the plan commission. “The performance standards for data centers require a minimum 200-foot setback from residential zone property and are maintained in the proposed site plan. Given that the property is primarily surrounded by interstate right-of-way, and adjacent to industrial and commercial use, a power generation facility would be appropriate at this site.” Peyton Childress, who spoke on behalf of the applicant at a recent plan commission meeting, said that the proposed development is a “behind-the-meter” solar project, with the power generated being used by the buildings on-site. “It will cover all of the energy needed for those five buildings, especially with the batteries on-site, because then during times where the sun is not out, then all of the stored energy from that solar array will be housed in the units of the battery and then can still power the facility itself,” she said. “So any excess energy we’re going to be storing in the battery containers and then we’ll use on-site. So no, I don’t foresee that we will be needing excess energy.” The five battery containers will be located behind the warehouses and out of sight of any potential tenants, she noted. “They do all have fire-suppression systems built in,” Childress said. “There’s a multitude of sensors that send warnings if any element of the container gets too hot, things like that.” According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, there have been lithium battery fires at some battery energy storage system (BESS) facilities. Such fires are very hard to put out and may reignite “hours or days later,” EPA officials said. These blazes can also release harmful gases. “Communities should also note that despite some high-profile incidents, improvements in BESS quality and design have led to a decrease in the number of failure incidents per gigawatt hour deployed,” the agency said. Planning and Development Director Bruce Knight said that fire safety is evaluated as part of the building permit review process. The fire department “has already looked at this development proposal and signed off on it with the assumption that it’ll comply with all building and fire codes,” he added. The subject property is located west of and across the street from 2612 N. Mattis Ave., where Research Press is based. Parkinson co-owns the book-publishing business with her brother and sister; the land on which the business sits is also owned by the family. In addition to fire safety, her other concerns include the facility’s proximity to residences east of her business and potential noise pollution. “They say that sometimes the data centers get noisy because of the cooling,” Parkinson said. Childress told the plan commission that the buildings will be “temperature-controlled.” “A lot of people are worried about water consumption as well, if that’s how we cool any of the server pods — none of that will be taking place here,” she said. “Any water on site would be bathroom or kitchen at inside of the commercial space. So these (data centers) would all be cooled by the temperature-controlled building.” She also noted that the developer will put in the vegetation screening that is required by the city. The proposed project comes as larger data-center developments have come under scrutiny. For instance, an advisory question on the April 6 ballot will ask Champaign County residents if the county should “support the development of large and/or hyperscale data centers, defined as larger than 10 megawatts of total power, within Champaign County.” The county currently has a moratorium on the development of data centers with “at least 10,000 square feet of processing area”; the ban is set to end in April. “They’re only 1.2 megawatts,” Trevino said of the data centers in the proposed project. “People usually consider a normal-size data center to be between 5 to 10 megawatts. Hyperscale’s more like starting at 100 megawatts. So really, this (project) could be seen more as a server room than what we think of as a data center.” Knight later added that the city is looking to impose a one-year moratorium on data centers over 10 megawatts so that staff can research the issue and develop ordinances. He expects the city council to vote on the one-year moratorium on Dec. 15. “Over 10 megawatts, based on our research, is where they start to have any kind of external impacts,” he said. artigo.texto: India's L&T wins battery storage order in Gujarat In a November 25 filing with the stock exchange, Larsen & Toubro LT (BSE: 500510), the Indian engineering conglomerate, disclosed that it has landed an order for a 300 MW/900 MWh battery storage installation in Khavda, located in Gujarat in the country's west. The facility will soak up excess electricity from renewable sources when output runs high and return it to the grid when consumption peaks. According to the company, this will allow more clean power to be absorbed into India's electricity network while making supply steadier and more dependable. The filing did not name the client or give the exact contract value. The order was won jointly by L&T Electronic Products & Systems (LTEPS) and the company's renewable energy unit, two divisions of the group. Offering 900 MWh of energy capacity alongside 300 MW of power output, the facility can run at maximum output for three hours. According to the filing, the system will rely on liquid cooling, an approach it anticipates will raise power density, improve safety and extend the installation's operating lifespan. L&T said the contract would bolster its standing in the energy storage business. The company added that the award showed clients were confident it could carry out large and complex projects. The Mumbai-based group describes itself as a $32bn multinational working across Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) projects, high-tech manufacturing, products and services in several countries. It has led its main business lines for eight decades, according to the filing.

artigo.texto: PL das baterias pode aumentar conta de luz em R$ 6,2 bi, diz entidade Frente dos Consumidores estima custo de cerca de R$ 94 bilhões em 15 anos e critica proposta que transfere aos consumidores despesas hoje atribuídas aos geradores O projeto de lei das baterias poderá acrescentar até R$ 6,26 bilhões por ano à conta de luz dos consumidores, segundo estimativa da FNCE (Frente Nacional dos Consumidores de Energia). O PL 3.716/2026 tramita em regime de urgência na Câmara dos Deputados e propõe mudar a divisão dos custos da contratação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia. De acordo com a entidade, a despesa poderia chegar a cerca de R$ 94 bilhões ao longo dos 15 anos previstos para os contratos dos leilões de baterias marcados para dezembro. O valor anual corresponde à estimativa de receita fixa que seria cobrada dos consumidores por meio do ERCap (Encargo de Reserva de Capacidade) para remunerar os sistemas contratados. O levantamento da FNCE considerou os preços-teto previstos nos editais e utilizou projeções da EPE (Empresa de Pesquisa Energética) como referência para estimar possíveis contratações de até 5 gigawatts (GW). O custo efetivo dependerá do volume contratado e dos preços obtidos nas disputas. A Lei 15.269/2025 estabeleceu que os custos da contratação de reserva de capacidade por meio de baterias devem ser rateados apenas entre os geradores de energia, conforme regulamentação da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). O projeto propõe retirar essa exclusividade, permitindo que a despesa seja dividida entre os consumidores. planalto.gov.br Para a FNCE, a mudança atingiria inclusive consumidores atendidos por distribuidoras que contratam majoritariamente energia de hidrelétricas e termelétricas. Na avaliação da frente, esses consumidores passariam a pagar por uma necessidade associada à intermitência de fontes como a solar e a eólica. O presidente da FNCE, Luiz Eduardo Barata, afirma que cabe aos geradores arcar com a contratação por considerar que eles são responsáveis pela necessidade de armazenamento. Segundo ele, a transferência da despesa para todos os consumidores pressionaria a inflação e elevaria a conta de luz, especialmente das famílias atendidas por distribuidoras com maior participação de hidrelétricas e térmicas em seus contratos. A Abeeólica (Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias) entrou na Justiça contra lei que impõe os custos. A entidade também pediu a suspensão dos dois leilões de reserva de capacidade. A FNCE, por outro lado, defende a manutenção do cronograma dos leilões e classifica como irresponsáveis as tentativas de suspensão das disputas. “Atrasar o leilão pode comprometer o enfrentamento dos cortes de energia e dificultar o equilíbrio do sistema. Não há justificativa técnica ou econômica para mudar o cronograma”, disse Barata, em nota. Os dois leilões estão previstos para 2 e 4 de dezembro, com contratos de 15 anos e início do suprimento em 1º de agosto de 2028. Ao aprovar os editais, a Aneel informou que os custos seriam rateados apenas entre os geradores, conforme a legislação vigente.

artigo.texto: The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space. SpaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind. The FCC’s approval requires that SpaceX launch its first data center satellite by 2030 and meet the 1 million mark by 2040. “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing. Is this actually safe?’” Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist who tracks satellite launches, told CNET. “It’s a blank check. Launch as many satellites as you can, and we’ll just see what happens. I think this is a mistake on the FCC’s part.” More from CNET Orbital data centers have long been a goal of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, becoming a pivotal part of his pitch to investors ahead of the company’s IPO in June. “You’re power-constrained on Earth. Space has the advantage that it’s always sunny,” Musk said in March. On its web page for Starmind, SpaceX touts its high-efficiency solar arrays on the planned satellites and the cooling benefits of space. It says that high-speed laser links will beam the AI results back to Earth through Starlink’s constellation. Space experts I’ve talked to this year about Starmind have been skeptical. The technical challenges alone are dizzying; the scale of SpaceX’s ambitions is hard to swallow. It’s taken seven years for Starlink to grow its constellation to 11,195 satellites, and that was already an unprecedented feat. Is it possible to get to 1 million satellites in 14 years? “We do not have the launch capacity for any of this,” Ian Christensen, senior director at the Secure World Foundation, told me in a previous interview. “Not even within SpaceX to do their own constellation, let alone the other constellations planned.” SpaceX has increasingly prioritized launching its own satellites instead of letting commercial customers hitch a ride on their rockets. Starlink’s share of SpaceX missions has gone from 54% of its Falcon 9 rocket’s missions in 2020 to about 79% in 2026, according to a Reuters analysis. One analysis estimates that SpaceX would have to launch 5,000 Starship rockets a year to meet its goal — a staggering increase from 330 rockets that launched last year in total. Scientists have already been ringing alarm bells about overcrowded orbits as they exist now. The more satellites in space, the more difficult it is for operators to maneuver around each other. A single crash could turn into decades of orbital debris, which could cause a chain reaction that eventually makes space inoperable for everyone. And burning up all those satellites in the atmosphere when they reach the end of their lives has already started to leave ozone-depleting aluminum particles behind. A paper published this week in Earth and Space Chemistry estimated that SpaceX’s data center plan would multiply pollutants in the upper atmosphere by more than 150 times compared to last year. “There are scientific papers out there raising issues,” McDowell said. “Yes, they’re unproven, but if I say, ‘Yeah, we’re not sure if this is going to destroy the atmosphere and kill us all, but it might,’ is the right reaction to go, ‘Well, you haven’t proven it, so we’re just going to ignore it’?” The FCC’s approval came despite objections from Amazon, the environmental nonprofit Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility and the American Astronomical Society. A representative for SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

artigo.texto: Group says data center neighbors should receive direct financial benefits MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WSFA) - A group that creates community benefit packages says people who live near data centers should receive a direct share of the profits as opposition to data centers grows. Meta is expanding its data center in Montgomery. In Lowndes County, residents packed city hall to oppose Project Red Clay. Benefit package proposal Janine Yorio of Community Digital Technologies said cities typically require something beneficial for the community in return for data center construction. She argued those long-term benefits do not always help everyone. “Data centers are not the most beautiful buildings in the world, but they also aren’t puffing out black smoke and creating traffic jams either,” Yorio said. “They are something that does bring a form of prosperity. And if the developers can figure out a way to transfer some of that prosperity locally, it can do a lot for a community.” Community Digital Technologies does not work directly with data centers or the people who oppose them. Yorio said the group creates and administers a benefits package. “So if people get something that looks like a credit card, and the credit card has the benefits on it, you can spend it,” Yorio said. “And it’s tied to when the data center opens. So obviously, both sides have to see both. They have to agree, and then they have to allow the data center to be built in the local neighborhood.” Yorio said making that kind of deal standard could turn data centers from a source of mistrust into a new stream of local prosperity. She said it would require buy-in from companies and local leaders. Meta said it has invested more than $1.5 billion in Montgomery. Cloverleaf, the developer behind Project Red Clay, has pledged up to $10 million to support Lowndes County. Residents respond Some Lowndes County neighbors said no amount of money can address their biggest concerns. “Do we feel there’s a need for money to come our way? Absolutely we do,” said John Urquhart, a Lowndes County resident. “If it drops in my backyard and my property values go away, we absolutely need to be compensated for that. But money’s not going to change the air quality issues, the noise pollution, the light pollution. Money’s not going to take care of any of that.” Urquhart said compensation would not change his outlook on the project. He cited air quality concerns related to diesel generators at operating data centers, as well as potential water contamination. Urquhart said he and his wife own 230 acres in the county. He said property values are falling and that some properties listed for sale in the area have not been viewed since they went on the market. Two Lowndes County women who are suing the Lowndes County Commission over Project Red Clay, a planned data center, are due back in court Dec. 2. Not reading this story on the WSFA News App? artigo.texto: Data center em órbita? SpaceX recebe autorização para 1 milhão de satélites Nova aposta da empresa de Elon Musk recebe aval do governo dos Estados Unidos e pode colocar constelação no espaço nos próximos 15 anos. A SpaceX recebeu autorização da FCC, órgão regulador análogo à Anatel nos Estados Unidos, para enviar até 1 milhão de satélites voltados para processamento de dados. A ideia da empresa é montar uma constelação de computadores na órbita da Terra, formando uma espécie de data center orbital para rodar, sobretudo, os trabalhos de IA ao redor do planeta. Os modelos enviados ao espaço seriam alimentados por energia solar, o que resolveria o alto consumo exigido desses servidores em Terra. Outra vantagem seria a baixa temperatura, que serviria para arrefecer as máquinas durante o processamento de dados. Da mesma forma, ao fragmentar esse trabalho em milhões de satélites, a geração de calor seria menor do que em Terra. Ainda assim, especialistas da área apontam diversos empecilhos para que os planos deem certo. Segundo a Associated Press, o astrofísico e autor Adam Becker classifica o projeto como uma “fantasia”, destacando problemas simples de física como impeditivos. A existência de vácuo, por exemplo, causaria retenção do calor gerado, independente da temperatura ao redor. Além disso, os riscos de colisão e poluição atmosféricas também são lembrados entre as críticas. Elon Musk já chegou a fazer parte do governo de Donald Trump, no início do segundo mandato. Apesar de desavenças, o magnata apoiou financeiramente candidatos do Partido Republicano de Trump nas eleições de meio de mandato. Recentemente, a SpaceX tem recebido diversas liberações para operar serviços de internet com a Starlink e até mesmo de telefonia, com a Starlink Mobile. Dessa vez, a aprovação da chamada constelação Starmind, veio com um comentário político: “os Estados Unidos estão liderando o mundo rumo à era da superinteligência”. Vale lembrar que Donald Trump oficializou a substituição do nome inteligência artificial para superinteligência (SI) em documentos do governo. Segundo ele, quem usa “IA” ao se referir à tecnologia é um “inimigo” dos EUA. Agora, a constelação de data center de Musk é classificada como “um novo passo” rumo a esse estágio dos LLMs. O pedido da SpaceX pela aprovação do envio da constelação à órbita da Terra recebeu diversos pedidos de veto, incluindo da Sociedade Americana de Astronomia e de empresas como Viasat e Kuiper Systems. Uma das preocupações é quanto à poluição visual do espaço aéreo, que pode atrapalhar a observação do céu tanto de entusiastas quanto de pesquisadores. Levar data centers para o espaço parece interessante a primeira vista, mas há algumas questões que preocupam cientistas e especialistas da indústria de computação. A possibilidade de fracionar o processamento é interessante, mas a grande quantidade de satélites exigidos para isso expõe todo o sistema ao risco de colisões em caso de algum mau funcionamento. Isso sem contar a grande quantidade já existente de lixo espacial na órbita terrestre. Outro ponto positivo seria a captação incessante de energia solar, o que tornaria o espaço “o lugar mais economicamente atrativo para instalar IA”, segundo Musk. Mas, segundo especialistas, o vácuo tornaria os módulos desse data center orbital muito mais suscetíveis a problemas. Sem refrigeração, um chip poderia superaquecer rapidamente, até mais que na Terra. Isso aconteceria pela retenção do calor na ausência de atmosfera. Um impedimento importante seria a dificuldade de realizar reparos via hardware, algo praticamente impossível pensando em 1 milhão de módulos menores. No final das contas, para além dos riscos e de toda improbabilidade apontada, um altíssimo investimento seria necessário para tentar driblar minimamente esses problemas. {{ excerpt | truncatewords: 35 }} {% endif %}

artigo.texto: A Justiça Federal do Distrito Federal rejeitou nesta 4ª feira (25.nov.2026) o pedido de liminar da Abeeólica (Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias) para suspender os leilões de armazenamento de energia em baterias, marcados para 2 e 4 de dezembro. A decisão é do juiz Diego Câmara Alves, da 17ª Vara Federal Cível do DF. Eis a íntegra (PDF – 57 kB). A entidade –que representa empresas de geração de energia eólica– havia ajuizado uma ação civil pública contra a União e a Aneel (Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica) em 16 de novembro. A associação argumenta que a contratação de baterias beneficia todo o sistema elétrico e que a atribuição dos custos exclusivamente aos geradores é inconstitucional. Questiona também a realização dos leilões antes da definição dos critérios de rateio dos encargos. O magistrado entendeu, porém, que a realização dos leilões não está condicionada à regulamentação da divisão de custos pela Aneel –que, ao atribuir a conta aos geradores, seguiu o que está determinado na lei. A decisão argumenta que não há risco de dano iminente aos geradores, uma vez que a cobrança do encargo terá início só em agosto de 2028. A suspensão dos leilões, por outro lado, poderia comprometer a segurança do fornecimento de energia elétrica. DISPUTA SOBRE QUEM PAGA A CONTA O impasse em torno dos leilões decorre da reforma do setor elétrico, sancionada em 2025, que atribui exclusivamente aos geradores os custos da contratação de baterias. Associações do setor elétrico articulam a aprovação do PL (Projeto de Lei) 3.716 de 2026 antes dos certames. De autoria do deputado Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania-SP), o texto retira a obrigação dos geradores e transfere os custos aos consumidores de energia. A proposta tramita em regime de urgência na Câmara dos Deputados e foi designada ao relator Danilo Forte (PP-CE) em 28 de outubro. Entidades que representam os consumidores são contrárias à mudança. A FNCE (Frente Nacional dos Consumidores de Energia) publicou estudo em que estima que a aprovação do projeto possa acrescentar até R$ 6,26 bilhões por ano à conta de luz. Paralelamente à articulação no Congresso, a Abeeólica acionou o STF (Supremo Tribunal Federal) em 19 de novembro. Diferentemente da ação civil pública, que busca impedir a realização dos leilões sob as regras atuais, a ADI (Ação Direta de Inconstitucionalidade) questiona diretamente a validade do dispositivo legal que atribui os custos aos geradores. O relator do processo, ministro Cristiano Zanin, ainda não analisou o pedido de liminar, segundo a decisão da Justiça Federal. https://www.poder360.com.br/poder-justica/justica-rejeita-pedido-de-eolicas-para-suspender-leilao-de-baterias/ ACERCA DEL CORRESPONSAL REDACCIóN CENTRAL Prensa Mercosur es un diario online de iniciativa privada que fue fundado en 2001, donde nuestro principal objetivos es trabajar y apoyar a órganos públicos y privados.

artigo.texto: Coloque a eixos nas suas fontes preferidas do Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Coloque a eixos nas suas fontes preferidas do Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. O Brasil chega aos primeiros leilões de baterias de grande porte com uma contradição. Ao mesmo tempo que reconhece a necessidade de armazenar energia para dar segurança ao Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), atribui exclusivamente aos geradores o custo desse serviço. A regra foi introduzida pela Lei nº 15.269/2025 e abre uma exceção ao modelo aplicado à reserva de capacidade das termelétricas, cujo custo é repartido entre os usuários finais do sistema. Se a disponibilidade de potência beneficia o conjunto da rede, qual é a justificativa para cobrar por ela de forma tão diferente? Uma bateria pode carregar quando há energia disponível e devolvê-la à rede no início da noite, quando a produção solar diminui e a demanda exige uma resposta rápida do sistema. Essa flexibilidade ajuda a atender aos horários de ponta, contribui para o controle de frequência e, quando o armazenamento é instalado em pontos estratégicos, pode aliviar gargalos de transmissão e reduzir cortes de geração. O benefício aparece na operação do SIN e na confiabilidade do fornecimento a quem depende dele. Em artigo publicado recentemente, o ex-senador e chairman do CERNE Jean Paul Prates chamou atenção para uma condição fundamental do princípio da causalidade econômica. Cobrar de quem provoca determinado custo exige demonstrar tecnicamente a origem desse custo. A variabilidade da geração eólica e solar é parte da equação, assim como o perfil do consumo, a expansão da geração distribuída com controle operacional limitado, as restrições de transmissão e a dificuldade de outras usinas de ajustar sua produção. No nordeste brasileiro, essa discussão tem efeito direto sobre a continuidade dos investimentos. Em determinados períodos, os cortes compulsórios de geração, conhecidos como curtailment, chegaram a superar a faixa de 15% a 20% da produção potencial em ativos eólicos e fotovoltaicos. Esses percentuais dimensionam perdas de geração. O impacto adicional do encargo dependerá da metodologia de rateio e dos valores contratados nos leilões. Para um parque que já perdeu receita, a nova despesa reduz a margem para honrar financiamentos e compromete a previsibilidade dos contratos de venda de energia de longo prazo. Para um projeto que ainda precisa passar pela decisão final de investimento, pode ser suficiente para adiar ou inviabilizar sua implantação. O efeito se estende aos fornecedores, aos empregos e à arrecadação dos municípios potiguares. Adiciona-se a isso um questionamento por parte dos investidores, sobre a necessidade da inclusão dos sistemas de armazenamento (BESS) nos regimes de incentivos tributários estaduais, sendo um fator expressivo no CAPEX dos projetos, e que pode comprometer a viabilidade dos investimentos. A indefinição também afeta os leilões previstos para 2 e 4 de dezembro. A Abeeólica pediu à Justiça Federal a suspensão dos certames, questionando a cobrança exclusiva dos geradores e os critérios de rateio em discussão na Aneel. Além do risco para o calendário, há um efeito sobre o preço. Como os sistemas de armazenamento exigem investimento elevado antes de começar a operar, os contratos precisam oferecer previsibilidade suficiente para viabilizar o financiamento. Se a fonte de pagamento está sujeita a litígio e recai sobre agentes já pressionados por perdas de receita, os investidores podem incorporar essa incerteza aos lances. Uma regra criada para concentrar a cobrança pode, assim, encarecer a própria contratação das baterias. Por isso, o CERNE defende a aprovação do PL nº 3.716/2026. O projeto revoga o dispositivo inserido pela Lei nº 15.269/2025 que atribuiu aos geradores o custeio exclusivo do armazenamento contratado como reserva de capacidade. Com a mudança, as baterias voltariam à regra geral de rateio entre os usuários finais, a mesma aplicada à potência contratada das termelétricas no LRCAP de 2026. São tecnologias com características operacionais distintas que, nesse contexto, atendem a uma necessidade comum do sistema. O tratamento do custeio deve refletir esse serviço. O consumidor pode sentir o custo nos dois cenários. Pela regra atual, os geradores tendem a incorporar a nova despesa às ofertas em futuros contratos no mercado livre e nos leilões do mercado regulado, na medida em que as condições de mercado permitirem. Com o projeto, o pagamento ocorre de forma explícita e previsível, por meio do encargo de reserva de capacidade. Essa previsibilidade pode reduzir o prêmio de risco nos lances. Na operação, as baterias também podem evitar, em determinadas horas, o acionamento de usinas de maior custo. O Nordeste precisa de armazenamento para aproveitar melhor a energia que já produz e oferecer condições de fornecimento a novos investimentos industriais e a atividades de demanda elevada, como os data centers, sendo uma oportunidade de preservar uma cadeia produtiva construída ao longo de anos e ampliar o uso econômico da sua geração renovável. Aprovar o PL antes dos certames daria ao primeiro ciclo de contratação de baterias uma base de custeio compatível com o serviço que o país espera delas. Darlan Santos é diretor-presidente do Centro de Estratégias em Recursos Naturais e Energia (CERNE)

artigo.texto: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites for AI data centers in space (AP) - The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk’s rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission lauded its authorization as a historic first amid the artificial intelligence race. It said that SpaceX’s one million “orbital compute modules” (forming a data center constellation called “Starmind”) would process massive amounts of data that would be used back on Earth — and bring humans closer to harnessing “the full power of the sun.” “America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, who was appointed by Republican President Donald Trump, said in a statement. He added that Wednesday’s move “opens a bold new frontier.” A lengthier authorization order published by the FCC noted that the company must deploy at least “one authorized space station” by 2033 — and then gradually add more and more through 2040. Musk welcomed the decision over social media. The world’s richest man has long vowed to form vast, solar-powered data centers in space to help run AI tools on Earth. But scientists and industry experts have stressed enormous technical and financial obstacles, as well as a host of environmental concerns. Adam Becker, an astrophysicist and author, called the prospect of launching a million satellites into space to create data centers “a fantasy.” “It’s not going to happen,” he said Wednesday. Proponents of data centers in space argue that capturing the sun’s energy would ease pressure on power grids and cut demand for sprawling computing warehouses on Earth (and resources like water needed to cool them). Space seems to offer a solution because it is cold, but it is also a vacuum, trapping heat inside objects much like a thermos. Becker explained that there are “basic physical limits” to otherwise radiating that heat out — and sending lots of smaller satellites could potentially carry the necessary material combined, but it would be expensive and difficult. He and others also point to additional risks, such as atmospheric pollution through launches and reentries, as well as possible in-orbit collisions that could impact other essential satellites. “You could end up with a cascading set of space junk collisions,” said Becker, noting such crashes could create “a cloud of debris” in the low Earth orbit — where many weather and telecommunication satellites are also found. In its ruling, the FCC maintained that SpaceX’s proposed Starmind constellation operates consistently with its orbital debris rules. It also acknowledged that it had received a “substantial number” of public comments leading up to its authorization Wednesday, including petitions to deny SpaceX’s request. But the regulator maintained that deploying the satellites “serves the public interest” — and said that it dismissed topics that it didn’t have authority over, such as environmental concerns. The American Astronomical Society, satellite communication company Viasat and Amazon-owned Kuiper Systems were among those who called on the regulator to deny SpaceX’s proposed data centers in space. In a statement Wednesday, the AAS said it was “disheartened and dismayed” by the FCC’s decision. The organization said that SpaceX’s proposed position of data centers in low Earth orbit would undermine decades of federal investment in astronomical facilities and “the ability of astronomers and the public to enjoy and study the night sky.” “The proposed constellation involves larger (and therefore brighter) and more numerous objects,” AAS said, noting that “these satellites would therefore be visible as extremely bright objects for longer periods in the night sky.” Becker echoed that sentiment. “It also is pollution of the night sky to the naked eye,” he said. Viasat, Amazon, SpaceX and the FCC did not immediately respond to The Associated Press’ requests for further comment Wednesday. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: The residents of Michigan's Ypsilanti Township are continuing to fight back against what they're calling a proposed "data center" after the University of Michigan's Board of Regents approved funding for a new research computing center last week. The board voted 7-1 on the $785 million construction costs for the $1.25 billion high-performances computing center intended for medical, science, clean energy, engineering and national security research. It's planned for a 124-acre site zoned for industrial use, with an additional 20 acres designated for a DTE electrical substation. The university said this project is not a data center or manufacturing site, but rather a "computing and research hub designed to advance science and education." University Promises Before the vote, University President Domenico Grasso said this project is "a critical step towards realizing one of the University of Michigan's most innovative and needed research initiatives." Read More on AI The university is partnering with Los Alamos National Laboratory and the state to deliver 50 megawatts of power initially, possibly expanding to 100 at full build-out, and is expected to "put Michigan at the forefront of the next generation of scientific discovery, which is where we always want to be." Grasso promised to work closely with the surrounding community to protect the environment, monitor utility usage and preserve the Huron River. He also said the board will commit $5 million over the next five years to the greater Ypsilanti area through its Community Partnership Program. "Leadership is not about pretending we know everything or have the perfect solutions; It is about listening and learning, recognizing where we can improve, and adjusting as appropriate," he said. "We want the people who live and work here to understand our motives and plans, and see the benefits of this partnership." In a letter to Congresswoman Debbie Dingell, Grasso said the university signed a Memorandum of Understanding in late 2024/2025 and said the Los Alamos has made no commitment of funds. “All activities require a separate agreement that will govern specific terms, conditions, funding and any other contractual obligations between U-M [the University of Michigan] and LANL [Los Alamos National Lab]," a spokesperson for Los Alamos told Newsweek. "There is no additional obligation between U-M and LANL. The classified computing center is not currently in the out years' NNSA [National Nuclear Security Administration] budget profile.” According to the Michigan Daily, Los Alamos confirmed that the facility would be used to research nuclear weapons. Community Backlash Critics of the project call it another data center that is set to disrupt the community and local environment. Residents and groups like Stop the Data Center have been protesting this facility for months. Reporting from Planet Detroit highlights outrage from residents, and promises from a local attorney to "use every legal means necessary to stop the data center." “U of M has gone far afield when it comes to the constitutional autonomy which they have enjoyed by virtue of being a university,” attorney Doug Winters said at a Thursday panel discussion. The United Tribes of Michigan (UTM) has also pushed back against the proposal, expressing its desire to preserve Native American cultural and heritage sites in the region and raised concerns about land use, noise levels, water consumption and electrical power needs. It also asked to be included in consultation about the facility's development. "Ypsilanti Township is along the Huron River in Southeastern Michigan and is located in an area that was used by Indian tribes for river and trail travel throughout history," UTM said in a resolution. "The area includes many sites of burials and other locations indicating indigenous usage and Ypsilanti Township is strongly concerned about a proposed data center within its boundaries, particularly about the potential impact on tribal cultural resources." In October, the university released a statement that it is conducting the appropriate due diligence and that a preliminary background search found "no evidence of archeological artifacts or culturally-sensitive materials found at the project site." Regent member Paul Brown, the only no vote, has joined community members protesting the facility. In August, he released a statement calling to stop the super computer site due to a lack of adequate community engagement. "When our development affects communities, we have to take responsibility to involve the people who live there," he said. "The university has failed to engage in an adequate conversation with those most affected and I cannot stand by and support this project being shoved down their throats, in a way that looks like environmental racism." The university is exempt from local building and zoning laws and does not pay property taxes. Michigan House Democrats introduced legislation in June to revoke the school's unilateral authority to circumvent zoning laws and town ordinances to buy land. “My community has been shaken by the university’s decision to quietly buy up land for the massive Los Alamos Data Center,” state Representative Jimmie Wilson of Ypsilanti said in a statement. “Every decision they’ve made was without consultation with local leaders or residents, and when the township board stood up and formally opposed it, U-M just ignored us and bulldozed ahead. "We are the ones who live here, pay taxes here and raise our kids here, but a multi-billion-dollar institution can just decide to drop a massive project in our backyard and expect us to deal with it," he said. "That is a complete betrayal of the public trust, and we’re putting a stop to it.” Local Community Impacts The university said the plan will not draw from or discharge into the Huron River or local groundwater and intends to protect local wildlife around the river. artigo.texto: A new study from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) finds that the expansion of data centers for artificial intelligence (AI) has had substantial negative health and air quality impacts — not just in the areas where most of these centers are being built, but also in regions far away from them. As a result, hundreds of people across the U.S. are dying annually, the study suggests, with researchers finding that pollution from electricity demands of data centers resulted in around 650 premature deaths in 2023 alone. Considering the rapid expansion of data centers since that time, the number could be even higher. “States hosting the largest data center loads do not necessarily experience the highest attributable mortality rates, while some states with little data center demand bear substantial burdens,” a summary of the study states. Researchers compared electricity that was generated from areas with data centers and those without them. They then modeled the electrical output increase due to data centers in both areas, monitoring air pollution rates in various areas of the country. Because the U.S. grid is interconnected, data center electricity demand is more spread out than many people realize. Different types of power plants also emit different amounts of pollution. So, while more data centers are being constructed in states like Virginia and Texas, Midwestern states, including Iowa, Nevada, South Dakota, and Kansas, are seeing higher per capita rates of death as a result of pollution from data centers. “When people think about the negative impacts of data centers, they usually focus on the neighbors,” said Noelle Selin, senior author of the study. “But our study indicates that the air quality impacts of data centers are very widespread across a large region.” “Even if you don’t think you are affected because there is not a data center near you, think again,” Selin added. In their findings for 2023, researchers found that data centers likely accounted for 513 premature deaths from fine particulate matter, while 137 deaths were associated with increases in ozone or fog that the data centers helped to create. A separate study published earlier this month also demonstrated the enormous output of electricity — and pollution — due to the explosive growth of data centers in the U.S. In that Harvard-based study, it was determined that data centers across the country emitted a total of 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide per year. That number is equivalent to the output of some countries, including Bolivia and Denmark. Much of the research amounted to “detective work,” the authors of the study said, due to lax federal requirements on public disclosure. “Communities shouldn’t need a team of Harvard researchers to analyze satellite images to understand their environmental impact,” said Harvard scientist Gianluca Guidi, who led the research team. artigo.texto: O Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN) aprovou em reunião desta quinta-feira, 26 de novembro, uma resolução que reduz o custo do financiamento do Fundo Clima para baterias com conteúdo nacional, conforme os critérios estabelecidos pelo Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES). A taxa saiu de 6,5% ao ano para 3%. Os recursos do Fundo Clima poderão financiar até 80% dos projetos ou 100% dos itens elegíveis, com teto de R$ 1 bilhão por grupo econômico a cada 12 meses. Para ter acesso direto ao crédito, o financiamento mínimo é de R$ 20 milhões. Para serem elegíveis às regras de conteúdo nacional, os os fabricantes precisam demonstrar capacidade industrial instalada no Brasil, atendimento a percentuais mínimos de conteúdo local e documentação comprobatória dos componentes, processos e insumos utilizados, entre outros. Segundo o presidente do BNDES, Aloizio Mercadante, a redução do custo do Fundo Clima vai ajudar a atrair novos fabricantes, o que tende a aumentar a capacidade produtiva e tecnológica do país a partir do leilão previsto para 2 de dezembro, quando haverá exigência de conteúdo nacional. Um segundo certame, sem a obrigação, será feito no dia 4 de dezembro. “Trata-se de importante medida do governo do presidente Lula para garantir a segurança energética e aprofundar o desenvolvimento industrial no país”, completou. Ontem, 25 de novembro, o BNDES fez um webinar para detalhar as regras de credenciamento e financiamento do certame, quando foi detalhada a forma de estruturação das operações nas modalidades project finance e crédito corporativo. No webinar, executivos do BNDES explicaram que o banco poderá flexibilizar os cronogramas de amortização e a estrutura de garantias dos financiamentos dos projetos com conteúdo nacional, com condições simplificadas para as rotas 2, 3 e 4. Apesar da possibilidade de customização, o banco sinalizou que os recursos do Fundo Clima deverão priorizar o ciclo inicial de investimentos, até a entrada em operação comercial definida pelo regulador. O vencimento do financiamento deve ocorrer seis meses antes do encerramento do contrato, que terá duração de 15 anos.

artigo.texto: WEG é credenciada pelo BNDES para leilão de armazenamento de energia A WEG obteve o credenciamento de seu pack de baterias de lítio junto ao Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) e está habilitada para o primeiro leilão de armazenamento de energia do Brasil. A disputa nacional, restrita a sistemas com requisitos de conteúdo local, está marcada para a quarta-feira (2). Com o registro, investidores que adotarem a solução da fabricante de Jaraguá do Sul (SC) passam a ter acesso a condições diferenciadas em linhas de financiamento, como a de Máquinas e Equipamentos e a do Fundo Clima. WEG é enquadrada na rota 2 de credenciamento A empresa foi classificada na rota 2, que exige etapas de fabricação dos packs no Brasil. A rota 1 permite importar as baterias. Dentro da rota 2, há diferenças de profundidade industrial: parte das soluções se limita a integrar módulos e conjuntos já montados, enquanto outras partem das células para processos mais complexos de fabricação e montagem. A classificação pesa no custo dos projetos. Em empreendimentos de grande porte, em que custo de capital, prazo de financiamento e previsibilidade de receitas são determinantes, a diferença tende a influenciar a escolha de fornecedores. Relembre: WEG terá nova fábrica para produção de sistemas de armazenamento de energia Para o diretor de Vendas Solar, BESS (sigla para sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias) e Building da WEG, Harry Schmelzer Neto, a empresa se diferencia justamente nessa etapa de fabricação. “É justamente nessa segunda abordagem que nos diferenciamos estrategicamente no mercado. A WEG está indo além da estratégia de nacionalização a partir das células e do atendimento regulatório, pois está contribuindo para estabelecer uma indústria brasileira de armazenamento com maior conteúdo tecnológico, competitividade e autonomia ao mercado”, afirmou o executivo. Sete empresas aparecem na lista de fornecedores do BNDES O BNDES credenciou sete empresas como fornecedoras de sistemas de armazenamento de energia para o leilão: WEG, Moura, You.On, TBEA, Gotion, Trina e BYD. Figurar na lista, porém, não significa que os equipamentos já sejam considerados nacionais. Os sistemas credenciados ainda passam por nova avaliação técnica do banco para comprovar o conteúdo local exigido. Confira também: Carga da WEG de 449 toneladas chega à BR-101 rumo ao Porto de Itajaí Leilão de baterias exige 15% de conteúdo local na disputa nacional A exigência mínima de conteúdo local para a modalidade nacional é de 15%. A Windey, outra fabricante chinesa, obteve credenciamento no BNDES para packs de baterias a serem montados em Camaçari (BA) e pretende oferecer sistemas à disputa nacional. A empresa estima atingir índice médio de nacionalização de 85%, contra o mínimo de 15% exigido. Datas da disputa e do prazo para o certificado do BNDES - 2 de dezembro de 2026: disputa de armazenamento nacional, restrita a sistemas com requisitos de conteúdo local - 4 de dezembro de 2026: disputa de armazenamento geral, sem exigência de nacionalização - 7 de maio de 2027: prazo, pela minuta de edital em consulta pública da Aneel, para os vencedores do Produto A apresentarem o certificado do BNDES, sob pena de não assinarem o contrato Fábrica de Itajaí e contratos ainda sem confirmação Os valores do investimento na nova fábrica de Itajaí, a capacidade de 4 GWh anuais e o início de operação no segundo semestre de 2027 não foram confirmados em outras fontes. O mesmo vale para os percentuais de financiamento pelo Fundo Clima, a duração de 15 anos dos contratos e o início de operação previsto a partir de agosto de 2028. Também não foi confirmado que a WEG tenha a homologação final dos sistemas para o leilão. A data em que o credenciamento da WEG foi concedido não aparece nas páginas consultadas. Reportagens sobre a lista de sete empresas, com a WEG incluída, já circulavam com datas anteriores, o que indica que o credenciamento não é novidade absoluta. A data do ato ainda não foi confirmada.
